messages.subject_clean: getting non-Ascii characters in and out of R unchanged
messages.body_plain:
Hello List,

 

I have a very simple programming task, which is adding ERP codes to input files for an EEG experiment.

That is not the problem.

 

However, the data contains non-ascii characters (see below) and I do not manage 

to get them in and out of R without changes. The files are originally .xlsx, but both readxlsx and readxl packages
seem to ‘normalize’ the input (so that the “ħ” becomes an “h”), and the original character is lost.

 

If I save the file as csv in Excel, and use read.csv, one of two things happens:

 

I use fileEncoding = “UTF-8” and again, the special characters are converted to their nearest ASCII neighbor.

I do not use fileEncoding and the non-ascii characters get garbled.

 

Any ideas how to get non-American characters in and out of R without such changes?

 

Best,

Holger

 

PS: An example of the input file:

 

Run order            Filename             Condition            OnsetADJ            OnsetChange    Question             Answer

1              MALTESEINCOR0032Idealista      MALINCONG     2.263     2.728     Mario iħobb jimmaġina?               Iva

2              MALTESEINCOR0032Grazzjuż     MALINCONG     1.615     2.048     Anita tisfen il-ballet?       Iva

3              SEMANOM20036gallettinaCor    SEMCONG          1.901                                     

 

 

-                      - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

-                      Prof. Holger Mitterer PhD (Maastricht)

-                      Department of Cognitive Science

-                      Faculty of Media and Knowledge Sciences

-                      +356 2340 3127

messages.body_plain:
Dear Martin and Jan,

 

thanks for the quick replies.

What systems are you working on?

 

I work on Windows, and I am not able to get it to work.

get locale gives “English_United States.1252” for all.
 
The Problem is that setlocale does not accept anything containing UTF-8,
so I can do Sys.setlocale("LC_ALL", "German")
but this only changes it to German_Germany.1252, or change it back to my original by:

Sys.setlocale("LC_CTYPE", "English_US.1252")

 
 
Anything containg UTF is rejected, both
Sys.setlocale("LC_ALL", "en_GB.UTF-8")
or the more restrictive
Sys.setlocale("LC_CTYPE", "en_GB.UTF-8")
 
return the message:

OS reports request to set locale to "en_GB.UTF-8" cannot be honored

 
I have not found a way to change the Character type local to anything that contains UTF8.
Any ideas?
 
Holger

messages.body_plain:
HI,

I don’t have Windows installed so I can’t check either, but I thought that the command Martin sent (or read_csv("unicode_text.csv",locale = locale(encoding = "UTF-8”)) for a CSV file) would work. 

Here’s some information about using csv files containing unicode into Windows. I got it to work during a workshop where some students on a Windows machine had problems reading Japanese text. Could you see whether that works for a CSV file with your data?  


https://dss.iq.harvard.edu/blog/escaping-character-encoding-hell-r-windows <https://dss.iq.harvard.edu/blog/escaping-character-encoding-hell-r-windows>

Also note the reference to a bug in Windows version of R that causes unicode to be displayed incorrectly (you’ll get the unicode representation rather than the character). 

Joe

messages.body_plain:
Hi Holger,
Some years ago I wrote about getting non-ASCII glyphs from Excel into R, in the
phonR tutorial vignette <http://drammock.github.io/phonR/>.  It's in the
last section before the acknowledgments (admittedly not easy to find).
Excerpting the relevant information here:

If you try to save a spreadsheet from Excel as plain CSV, all the non-ASCII
glyphs will converted to a ? character. If you export from Excel as
“Unicode text”, what you get is tab-separated values encoded in “UCS2-LE”
format (AKA, “UTF-16 little-endian with BOM”). The easiest route to opening
this in R is to first convert it to UTF-8 (e.g., by opening in the free
text editor Notepad++ <https://notepad-plus-plus.org/>, using the
“Encoding” menu, then re-saving), and then read into R using
read.delim(..., sep='\t').

I don't know if this is the only way; I've not tried the various packages
designed to read Excel files directly.
-- dan

Daniel McCloy
http://dan.mccloy.info/
Postdoctoral Research Associate
Institute for Learning and Brain Sciences
University of Washington
